body:
Rust 1.86 reaches `quotes.rs` and fails with E0658 because the crates do not declare the Rust 1.87 requirement of `usize::is_multiple_of`. Both published manifests now declare `rust-version = "1.87"`, allowing Cargo to report the required compiler before compilation and MSRV-aware resolvers to select compatible releases.

Fixes #334.

The Rust workflow builds and runs the full workspace tests on 1.87.0 and stable, including parser tests without the optional macro. A separate 1.86.0 job checks Cargo's rejection diagnostic for the parser with and without macros and for the standalone macro crate. Matrix jobs use distinct concurrency groups, and publishing requires both the test matrix and the rejection check. Both Rust READMEs document the MSRV.

This branch merges `main` at `5b05ceb`, including PR #336's JavaScript document APIs and PR #335's lossless reference handling. The 14 release metadata conflicts are resolved by preparing `links-notation` **0.25.1** after main's 0.25.0, with `links-notation-macro` **0.1.1**. All seven implementation versions, installation snippets, package locks, benchmark dependencies and the generated report remain consistent with the repository's mandatory release check.

Reproduction and regression:

```sh
rustup toolchain install 1.86.0 1.87.0 --profile minimal
bash experiments/issue-334/check-msrv.sh
cd rust
cargo +1.87.0 build --release
cargo +1.87.0 test
cargo +1.87.0 test -p links-notation --no-default-features
```

The regression failed before the fix with the issue's E0658 at `quotes.rs:131`; it now passes all three cases with `requires rustc 1.87`. See [the reproduction instructions](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/blob/issue-334-afb384d6aaae/experiments/issue-334/README.md). The declaration records the existing compiler requirement. Already published versions retain their old metadata.

Validation on the merged tree:

- All seven language test suites; Rust workspace tests and parser tests without macros on 1.87.0 and stable, plus the 1.86.0 rejection regression.
- Rust formatting and Clippy with all targets/features and warnings denied; JavaScript formatting, lint, build, TypeScript declarations, the document example and 2,380 reference/document round trips; Python, Go, Java, C# and PHP lint/format checks.
- Release consistency, generated test comparison, benchmark report/datasets, binary interoperability, documentation comparison and website build.
- actionlint, ShellCheck, registry probe tests, zizmor, dependency freshness and compatible transitive npm/Bun lock checks.

CI validation on commit `2ff6937c37c87e7db77f821358dc313c172206fa`: **all 63 checks passed**, with 17 expected publication/conditional skips. [Rust CI](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/actions/runs/37857215328) passes both toolchains and the 1.86 rejection regression. Language suites, binary interoperability, benchmarks, security, dependency freshness, workflows, links, documentation and the C# PDF artifact check are green. GitHub reports the branch as mergeable with no conflicts.
